subject: How to fix mean and variance of latent variables with confmirt()?

messages.author: f7496b4b5a97437e
messages.subject: How to fix mean and variance of latent variables with confmirt()?
parts:
Hi,
I would like to know how to fix the mean and variance of the latent variables when specifying a model with confmirt.model().

Cheers, Jens

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to fix mean and variance of latent variables with confmirt()?
parts:
This question was migrated from Cross-Validated, so here's the
background syntax that was proposed:

####

require(mirt)

# Generate the data

a <- matrix(c(1, NA, NA, 1, NA, NA, NA, 1, NA, NA, 1, NA, NA, NA, 1, NA, NA, 1),
ncol=3, byrow=TRUE)

d <- matrix(c(-1, NA, 1, NA, -1, NA, 1, NA, -1, NA, 1, NA), ncol=2,
byrow = TRUE)
type = c("dich", "dich","dich","dich","dich","dich")

simdat <- simdata(a, d, 100, itemtype = type)

# Specify the model

model1 <- confmirt.model()
1: F1 = 1 - 2
2: F2 = 3 - 4
3: F3 = 5 - 6
4: COV = F1*F2, F1*F3, F2*F3
5: SLOPE = F1@1 eq 1, F1@2 eq 1, F2@3 eq 1, F2@4 eq 1, F3@5 eq 1, F3@6 eq 1

#Fit the model

c_model1 <- confmirt(simdat, model1)

####

Looking at this it appears you are using a much older version of mirt,
and the current version on CRAN is version 0.9.0. The latest doesn't
include the confmirt.model() or confmirt() functions, and instead have
either been renamed (mirt.model()) or can be accessed by a method
argument(confmirt(...) is now the same as mirt(..., method = 'MHRM')).
Also I dropped support for the SLOPE, INT, and PRIOR arguments in the
original article since I found them to be a bit cumbersome and not
very R like. I'd recommend checking out the examples on Github for
getting a feel for the new package layout, and there are a handful of
exercises and examples that have been worked through there.

To get you started after you update to version 0.9.0, you want to edit
the starting values directly, so passing sv <- mirt(data, model, pars
= 'values') will give a data.frame called sv containing all the
starting values and whether they are estimated. Modify this object to
your liking (you can use the sv <- edit(sv) function if you prefer to
use a GUI) and pass this back into the estimation function with
mirt(data, model, pars = sv). Hope that helps.

Phil
